creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`docs/red/README.md` links twelve REDs. Three have no file behind them: RED-8 (Interactivity as a first-class capability, listed Implemented), RED-C (Own our interactivity layer, Draft), RED-D (One artifact for bundling and standalone executables, Draft). `git ls-files docs/red/` confirms they were never committed, so this isn't local drift.

`docs/red/STYLE.md` tells readers to study RED-C as the model for a live draft, so the style guide points at one of the missing files.

Worth folding two corrections back into `docs/VISION.md` while here: §5.4 and Appendix A both cite "RED-D stub" as an existing artifact, and §7 cites AI_POLICY.md as saying "verification over generation", a phrase that doesn't appear in it. The actual text (`AI_POLICY.md:15,22`) requires PRs be "fully verified with human-in-the-loop" - same spirit, but don't quote the invented version in public copy.

---

### Orientation

- REDs are decision records under `docs/red/`. `docs/red/README.md` holds the hand-maintained index table; the three broken links are `0008-interactivity.md`, `C-radish.md`, and `D-bundle-and-compile.md`. `git ls-files docs/red/` confirms nine committed documents plus `README.md`, `STYLE.md`, `template.md`, and `backfill-plan.md` - the three were never committed, so this is not local drift.
- The process is itself a RED: `docs/red/0001-red-process.md`. Read it first.
- `docs/red/template.md` is the skeleton to copy - YAML frontmatter (`red`, `title`, `status`, `kind`, `created`, `decided`, `released`, `supersedes`, `superseded-by`, `related`) then Summary, Context/Motivation, Decision, Rationale, Alternatives Considered, Compatibility & Migration, Other Consequences & Trade-offs, optional Future Directions / Open Questions / References, and a History list.
- `docs/red/STYLE.md` owns voice and prose. Note the circularity: STYLE.md:7 and STYLE.md:43 both direct readers to study RED-C as the model live draft, and RED-C is one of the missing files. Either write RED-C first or fix STYLE.md's pointer.

### Where to start

The three are not the same kind of job.

- **RED-8 (Interactivity, status Implemented)** is a *backfill* - the decision already shipped, so it is reconstructed from git history and the codebase. `docs/red/backfill-plan.md` is the existing plan for exactly this and should be read before starting. The `red-archaeologist` skill exists for this workflow: archaeology through git and the code first, then a numbered interview with the maintainer, then the write-up. Do not skip the interview - the *why* is the part that is not in the diff. Source material: the `RInteractive` seam in `core/global.go`, plus `core/interactive.go`, `core/input.go`, `core/func_pick.go`, `core/func_multipick.go` and `docs/funcs/input.md`. Note `confirm` has no file of its own - it is registered in `core/funcs.go` like the other small builtins.
- **RED-C (Own our interactivity layer, status Draft)** and **RED-D (One artifact for bundling and standalone executables, status Draft)** are forward-looking drafts. Archaeology will not produce them - they need the maintainer's current intent. Interview, do not excavate. Source material: RED-C - `go.mod:13` pins `github.com/amterp/radish v0.2.0`, checkout at `~/src/radish`; RED-D - `docs/thinking/bundling.md`, `.goreleaser.yml`, and `docs/VISION.md:130` which calls `rad build` "planned as RED-D".

**Fold in the VISION.md corrections while here** (all verified):

- `docs/VISION.md:269`, in §5.4 - "RED-D exists as a stub; it should be written for real". Once RED-D exists, this sentence is wrong.
- `docs/VISION.md:516`, in Appendix A - lists "docs/red/ (especially RED-2, RED-6, RED-D stub)" under Internal state. Same fix. (There is a third RED-D reference at line 368, in the §6 Phase 3 roadmap table; it reads as a forward plan and is fine as-is.)
- `docs/VISION.md:418`, in §7 - claims `AI_POLICY.md` "has said 'verification over generation' since before this document". That phrase does not appear in `AI_POLICY.md`. The actual text is "Pull requests created by AI must have been fully verified with human use" (`AI_POLICY.md:16-17`) and a human-in-the-loop requirement for issues and discussions. Same spirit, but the quote is invented and this is public-facing copy - paraphrase or quote the real line.

### How to verify

```sh
make build
git ls-files docs/red/                       # every link in README.md's index must appear here
./bin/radd example.rad                       # run any Rad snippet you put in a RED
make test
```

Check every link in `docs/red/README.md` resolves, and that each new file's frontmatter `status` matches the status column in the index table.

### Done when

- `docs/red/0008-interactivity.md`, `docs/red/C-radish.md`, and `docs/red/D-bundle-and-compile.md` exist and are committed, with frontmatter matching `template.md` and statuses matching the index.
- Every link in the `docs/red/README.md` index resolves.
- `docs/red/STYLE.md` no longer points at a file that does not exist.
- The three `docs/VISION.md` corrections are made.
- Alternatives Considered is filled in for all three. `template.md` calls it the highest-value section, and it is the first thing that gets skipped.

### Watch out for

`docs/` is not a snippet root - `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go:42-45` covers only `docs-web/docs` and `core/error_docs`. Rad code in a RED is **not** executed by the test suite, so nothing catches a wrong example. Run anything you write through `./bin/radd` by hand.

RED-8 is marked Implemented in the index. Write it as the record of a decision already made, in past tense, with the Open Questions section empty - `template.md` says Open Questions should be heavy while Draft and empty by Implemented. Do not turn a backfill into a fresh proposal.
title: Write the three REDs that the index promises
